title: russias ozon says four logistics hubs targeted by ukrainian drones 2026 08 24
text:
Aug 24 (Reuters) - Four logistics hubs owned by Russia's second-largest online retailer Ozon ​in southern Russia were targeted in Ukrainian ‌drone attacks, the company said on Monday, bringing the number of targeted facilities to six since August 22.
Ozon said its ​logistics hub in Makhachkala, Dagestan, was on ​fire after a drone attack, while workers at ⁠warehouses in Adygeysk, in the Adygeya region, and ​Nevinnomyssk, in the Stavropol region, had been evacuated.
"According to ​preliminary information, several people were injured," Ozon said in a statement, referring to the facility in Makhachkala, which had halted operations.
The ​company also said a large fire broke out ​at its facility in the town of Enem in the ‌Krasnodar ⁠region. It added that facilities in Adygeya and Stavropol were not damaged.
Shares in Ozon fell by as much as 12% on the Moscow Exchange on news ​of the attack, ​while shares ⁠in its major shareholder, private equity firm AFK Sistema, fell by almost 13%.
Ozon ​has become Russia's second e-commerce giant, after ​rival ⁠Wildberries, to be targeted in Ukrainian drone attacks. Work at a logistics centre in the Samara region was ⁠halted ​after the first Ukrainian strike ​on the company's facilities on August 22.
